definitions.definition: Ttor = reals/(2*pi*integers), with normalized measure dx/(2*pi); spatial products and integrals are on this domain.
For an integrable periodic f, Fourier(f)(k)=hat f(k)=(2*pi)^(-1) integral_0^(2*pi) f(x) exp(-i*k*x) dx; the transform extends to distributions by duality.

For every real s, H^s(Ttor) is the completion of trigonometric polynomials with ||f||_(H^s)^2=sum_(k in Z) <k>^(2*s)|hat f(k)|^2, <k>=(1+k^2)^(1/2). Negative spaces are interpreted as distributions. Homogeneous norms on zero-mean distributions are ||f||_(dot H^s)^2=sum_(k!=0)|k|^(2*s)|hat f(k)|^2. Real means hat f(-k)=conjugate(hat f(k)); mean zero means hat f(0)=0.

L2=H^0(Ttor), with ||f||_2^2=(2*pi)^(-1) integral |f|^2 dx. More generally L^p uses the same normalized measure; L^infinity is essential supremum. Sequence ell^2 uses counting measure on Z (or Z\{0} when specified). Time suprema use continuous representatives; derivative norms are essential suprema.
For tau>0 and real alpha,beta, M_tau g=tau^(-1) integral_0^tau g(s) ds and eta_tau(alpha,beta)=M_tau(exp(-i*s*(alpha+beta)))-M_tau(exp(-i*s*alpha))*M_tau(exp(-i*s*beta)).

definitions.type: averaged cubic trilinear Fourier family, initially on polynomials
definitions.definition: For tau>0, t0 real, and mean-zero polynomial inputs f1,f2,f3, define Remainder_(t0,tau)(f1,f2,f3) to have zero mean and, for k!=0, Fourier coefficient -tau/(18*i*k) sum_(a+b+c=k,a+b!=0) exp(-i*t0*Phi)*eta_tau(alpha,beta)*hat f1(a)*hat f2(b)*hat f3(c), where p=a+b, alpha=3*a*b*p, beta=3*k*c*p and Phi=alpha+beta=k^3-a^3-b^3-c^3. Its bounded extensions will be proved; R^n_(2,tau) means t0=t_n.
For nonzero integers a,b,c,d with a+b+c+d=0, let N1>=N2>=N3>=N4 be the decreasing rearrangement of |a|,|b|,|c|,|d|, and Third(a,b,c,d)=N3. Ties may be ordered arbitrarily.

inputs.statement: For tau>0 and real alpha,beta, eta_tau=0 if alpha*beta=0; otherwise |eta_tau|<=2 min(|alpha/beta|,|beta/alpha|) and |eta_tau|<=tau min(|alpha|,|beta|). For nonzero integers a+b+c+d=0, with decreasing magnitudes N1>=N2>=N3>=N4, one has N1<=3N2 and, putting A=|ab|,B=|cd|, (1/|d|)min(A/B,B/A)<=3/N3 and |a+b|/max(A,B)<=6/N3.

For all nonnegative sequences x1,x2,x3,x4 in ell^2(Z\{0}), sum_(a+b+c+d=0,abcd!=0) x1(a)x2(b)x3(c)x4(d)/Third(a,b,c,d)<=C product_(r=1)^4||xr||_(ell^2). The same bound holds after restricting the sum to any subset.

output.statement: Remainder has a unique continuous trilinear extension from mean-zero H^sigma inputs to L2 for each 0<=sigma<=1, and ||Remainder_(t0,tau)(f1,f2,f3)||_2<=C_sigma*tau^(1+sigma)*product_j||fj||_(H^sigma), uniformly for all t0 real, tau>0 and Fourier support. The same estimate holds with any extra frequency multiplier of modulus <=1, including restrictions Phi=0 or Phi!=0. In particular if mean-zero w in H^gamma, mean-zero f in L2, ||w||_(H^gamma)<=M0 and delta=||f-w||_2<=1, then for 0<tau<=1, ||Remainder_(t0,tau)(f,f,f)||_2<=C_(M0,gamma)*tau*(tau^gamma+delta).

argument.text: Assume L1: 0<=sigma<=1, tau>0 and t0 real. Only nonzero a,b,c,k and p=a+b!=0 need be considered in the Fourier sum. Put d=-k, A=|ab| and B=|cd|; |alpha/beta|=A/B. N002 gives |eta|/|k|<=6/Third. Its second covariance bound gives |eta|/(tau|abck|)<=3|p|*min(A,B)/(AB)=3|p|/max(A,B)<=18/Third. The geometric mean with weights 1-sigma,sigma is |eta|/(|k| |abc|^sigma)<=6^(1-sigma)*18^sigma*tau^sigma/Third. This includes sigma=0,1. Zero input frequencies give eta=0 and the output k=0 was defined to vanish.

produces.statement: For all integers a,b,c,k with a+b+c=k, abck!=0 and a+b!=0, set alpha=3ab(a+b), beta=3kc(a+b). Under L1, |eta_tau(alpha,beta)|/(|k||abc|^sigma)<=6^(1-sigma)18^sigma tau^sigma/Third(a,b,c,-k).

argument.text: For polynomial f1,f2,f3 in H^sigma, dualize the Fourier formula against any finite ell2 sequence. Set x1(a)=|a|^sigma|hat f1(a)|, x2 and x3 analogously, and x4(d) equal to the absolute dual coefficient at -d. Taking absolute values removes exp(-i*t0*Phi), whose modulus is one. F001 and N003 bound the pairing by C_sigma*tau^(1+sigma)*product_j||fj||_(H^sigma)*||dual||_ell2, including the factor 1/18. Ell2 duality proves the stated norm bound. A multiplier of modulus <=1 only decreases this absolute envelope, so the estimate includes arbitrary restrictions.

produces.statement: Under L1, for the mean-zero polynomial inputs f1,f2,f3 and any extra multiplier with modulus <=1, ||Remainder_(t0,tau)(f1,f2,f3)||_2<=C_sigma tau^(1+sigma) product_j||fj||_(H^sigma).

argument.text: Polynomials are dense in H^sigma by its definition. The trilinear estimate bounds differences by a sum of three terms, each with one difference input and two bounded inputs. Thus polynomial approximations produce a Cauchy sequence in complete L2 with a unique limit independent of approximations; this defines the continuous extension and retains the estimate. Discharge L1 and quantify over all parameters and inputs.

produces.statement: For every real r in [0,1], t_aux real, tau_aux>0 and mean-zero g1,g2,g3 in H^r, the extension exists and ||Remainder_(t_aux,tau_aux)(g1,g2,g3)||_2<=C_r tau_aux^(1+r) product_j||gj||_(H^r), also with any extra multiplier of modulus <=1.

argument.text: H002 gives 0<gamma<=1. Under the final claim's conditions use F003's exponent-gamma bound on (w,w,w). For the difference use the telescoping trilinear expansion Remainder_(t0,tau)(f,f,f)-Remainder_(t0,tau)(w,w,w)=Remainder_(t0,tau)(f-w,f,f)+Remainder_(t0,tau)(w,f-w,f)+Remainder_(t0,tau)(w,w,f-w), each at the same t0,tau, and the exponent-zero bound. Its norm is <=C*tau*delta*(||f||_2+||w||_2)^2. Since ||f||_2<=M0+1, this is <=C_M0*tau*delta; the pure w term is <=C_(M0,gamma)*tau^(1+gamma). For 0<tau<=1 this proves the required numerical-state estimate without a numerical H^gamma bound.
